THE ANALYST'S TAKE

What the full dataset suggests

These findings always refer to the full six-month dataset, regardless of the filters above.

01 / GROWTH

A shorter month can hide stronger daily sales.

February's total net sales fell 4.7%, while sales per calendar day increased 5.5%. January-to-June daily sales rose 39.8%.

Business question

Track sales per operating day before interpreting a change in monthly totals.

Source: monthly_kpis.csv · SQL Q02
02 / CAPACITY

Saturday carries more than twice Monday's volume.

Saturday averaged 121.3 completed checks per day, versus 57.9 on Monday. Friday and Saturday evenings have longer modeled service times.

Proposed test

Trial peak service coverage and monitor time to service alongside labor cost and guest feedback.

Source: weekday_performance.csv · SQL Q05–06
03 / MENU

Beverages bring margin. Mains bring volume.

Beverages returned a 74.9% ingredient contribution margin, versus 63.9% for mains. Margherita Pizza led item net sales.

Proposed test

Test relevant beverage suggestions and measure contribution per check, not just sales.

Source: category_performance.csv · SQL Q03–04
04 / PROMOTIONS

Discount comparisons are not discount effects.

Discounted checks averaged $67.51 versus $77.84 at full price. Discounts were more common on quieter weekdays.

Proposed test

Use a controlled promotion test before estimating incremental demand or removing offers.

Source: discount_performance.csv · SQL Q08

BUILT TO BE EXPLAINED

Metric definitions & boundaries

Where does this data come from?

A fictional single-location restaurant: 15,102 recorded checks and 74,590 item lines across January–June 2026. All records are generated with a fixed seed. Demand growth, price changes and evening service delays are designed assumptions, not real-world evidence. This portfolio case was assembled with AI assistance.

How are sales and contribution calculated?

Gross sales = quantity × historical unit price. Each line's discount is rounded half up to cents, then subtracted. Contribution = net sales − historical ingredient cost. Contribution excludes labor, rent, waste and other overhead; it is not operating profit. Cancelled checks contribute no sales or ingredient cost.

What changes when I filter a category?

Sales and contribution include only matching item lines. Check count is the number of distinct completed checks containing those items. Average check becomes category spend per matching check, not the full basket value. Demand and service use those same distinct checks. Cancellations use period and channel only.

How are busy periods compared fairly?

Weekday demand divides checks by all occurrences of that weekday in the selected calendar period. Hourly cells divide by the same operating-day count. The restaurant is modeled as open every day; this avoids overcounting a weekday simply because it appears more often in the calendar.

What was verified, and what remains limited?

The Python analysis passed seven tests covering data integrity, cancellation treatment, currency rounding, independent reconciliation and seeded reproduction. Website calculations are checked against the project data. Native MySQL execution is pending; the repository includes a verifier. No recommendations were implemented and no revenue uplift or savings were measured.
